Feng Yi never thought he would one day become the River Master. Not when he hawked dried fish as a boy. Not when he saw the Khitan invade. Not even when the floodwaters rose high enough to drown the sky; Not everyone is born to be the hero of a storybook. He is not the kind who saves the world, and certainly not some imagined god. Because it isn't worth it. People aren't born to live for others. Roaming in this vast and indifferent world, in the end, we all come and go alone. We live, always, for ourselves.
That's why Feng Yi never understands her. Never understands the one in the world most skilled at getting herself into trouble. Never understands why, when the Zhang family entrusted her with a child, she chose to wear the River Master's mask. She is just a mortal. So why pretend to be an immortal? Why gild herself in myth, coat herself in mud, and become a clay idol for others to worship?"
A Yu... was it worth it?" Feng Yi finally asked.
She only smiled, eyes fixed on the shimmering currents of the Yellow River.
"Maybe," she said, "one day, what isn't worth it... will be."
And perhaps that day does come in the form of freezing rain from a colorless sky, of floodwaters surging higher than walls can hold, of city gates that will not open, and of her, collapsing lifeless into Feng Yi's arms.
"Ah Yu," he whispered, "It wasn't worth it. This world... it's not worth it."
